# **Omega Document Creator - Office PC Installation**

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Staff use one address inside and outside the office:

<https://omega-app.omegafinancial.ie>

They enter an approved email address, receive a Cloudflare email code, and then sign in to Omega using their individual Omega account.

##

## **Important: do not install the current branch as the live system**

The GitHub repository currently has no production release tag. The latest available security-fixes-2 branch remains at commit 80ab0d6 and still has production blockers.

Before this procedure is used with real client information, a tested release such as v1.0.0 must include:

- Secure creation of the first administrator.
- Enforced password changes and session revocation.
- Reliable client, dependant, quotation and autosave persistence.
- A production frontend build instead of Vite's development server.
- Safe offline backup restoration.
- Passing frontend, backend and PostgreSQL integration tests.

The developer should merge the approved code into main and create a GitHub release tag. Do not install directly from a feature branch.

## **1\. Prepare the office PC**

Use a dedicated Windows 11 Pro computer with:

- At least 16 GB RAM.
- At least a 500 GB SSD.
- Wired internet connection.
- BitLocker enabled.
- A UPS battery backup.
- BIOS virtualisation enabled.
- Windows and antivirus updates installed.
- Sleep and hibernation disabled.
- Automatic restart after power failure enabled in the BIOS, if supported.

Create a dedicated Windows account named something like:

OmegaServer

Only the server administrator should know this account's password. Staff should never work directly on this PC.

### **Disable sleep**

Open:

Settings → System → Power & battery

Set sleep to **Never** while plugged in.

Do not enable automatic Windows sign-in. After a restart, the server administrator must sign in and can then lock the screen. Docker Desktop and OneDrive need the dedicated account to remain signed in.

## **2\. Install WSL2**

Open PowerShell as Administrator and run:

wsl --install

Restart the computer. Sign back into OmegaServer, reopen PowerShell as Administrator and run:

wsl --update

wsl --version

Microsoft documents wsl --install as the standard Windows installation method. [Microsoft WSL installation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install)

## **3\. Install Git and Docker Desktop**

Open PowerShell as Administrator:

winget install --id Git.Git -e --source winget

winget install --id Docker.DockerDesktop -e --source winget

Restart Windows if requested.

Open Docker Desktop and enable:

- **Use the WSL 2 based engine**.
- **Start Docker Desktop when you sign in**.

Confirm the installation:

git --version

docker version

docker compose version

Docker recommends an up-to-date WSL installation for its Windows WSL2 backend. [Docker Desktop for Windows](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/windows-install/) · [Docker WSL2 guidance](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/features/wsl/)

Confirm that Omega meets Docker Desktop's business-use licensing conditions before deployment.

## **4\. Configure OneDrive client storage**

Sign in to OneDrive for Business using the dedicated server account.

Create the client folder. Replace the example OneDrive path with the exact path shown on the PC:

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "C:\\Users\\OmegaServer\\OneDrive - Omega Financial\\Omega Document Creator\\Clients"

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "C:\\OmegaData\\Backups"

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "C:\\OmegaApps"

In File Explorer:

1. Find Omega Document Creator\\Clients.
2. Right-click the folder.
3. Select **Always keep on this device**.
4. Confirm the solid green circle with a white tick appears.

This ensures the files remain local while also synchronising with OneDrive. [Microsoft OneDrive Files On-Demand](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/onedrive/save-disk-space-with-onedrive-files-on-demand-for-windows)

Do not put the following inside OneDrive:

- PostgreSQL database files.
- Docker volumes.
- The Git repository.
- .env.
- Cloudflare credentials.
- Database backup working files.

OneDrive synchronisation is not a complete backup. Deletions or ransomware damage can also synchronise.

## **5\. Download the approved GitHub release**

The GitHub repository should be private.

Open ordinary PowerShell:

Set-Location C:\\OmegaApps

git clone <https://github.com/EmeraldPathways/OmegaDocumentCreator.git>

Set-Location .\\OmegaDocumentCreator

git fetch --tags

git tag --list

Git may open a browser and ask you to authenticate with GitHub.

When the approved tag exists, install that exact release:

git switch --detach v1.0.0

git rev-parse --short HEAD

git status

Record the displayed commit number.

The office PC must never run directly from main, security-fixes-2 or a feature branch. GitHub releases identify the exact version installed. [GitHub Releases](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/managing-releases-in-a-repository)

## **6\. Create the production configuration**

Copy the example:

Copy-Item .env.example .env

notepad .env

Use the following structure, replacing every placeholder:

\# Database

POSTGRES_DB=omega

POSTGRES_USER=omega

POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REPLACE_WITH_LONG_RANDOM_ALPHANUMERIC_PASSWORD

DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://omega:REPLACE_WITH_SAME_PASSWORD@postgres:5432/omega

\# File storage

CLIENT_FILES_HOST_PATH=C:/Users/OmegaServer/OneDrive - Omega Financial/Omega Document Creator/Clients

BACKUPS_HOST_PATH=C:/OmegaData/Backups

FILE_STORAGE_PATH=/data/clients

BACKUP_PATH=/data/backups

\# Security

SESSION_SECRET=REPLACE_WITH_AT_LEAST_64_RANDOM_CHARACTERS

SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=30

COOKIE_SECURE=true

COOKIE_SAMESITE=lax

\# Public address

APP_URL=<https://omega-app.omegafinancial.ie>

ENVIRONMENT=production

REMOTE_ACCESS_MODE=remote

CORS_ORIGINS=<https://omega-app.omegafinancial.ie>

CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=<https://omega-app.omegafinancial.ie>

TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT=1

\# First administrator

ADMIN_EMAIL=YOUR_INDIVIDUAL_ADMIN_EMAIL

ADMIN_PASSWORD=REPLACE_WITH_UNIQUE_INITIAL_PASSWORD

\# Backup schedule

BACKUP_SCHEDULE_ENABLED=false

BACKUP_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL_MINUTES=1440

\# AI

AI_ENABLED=false

LOCAL_AI_ENABLED=false

Important:

- Use the same database password in POSTGRES_PASSWORD and DATABASE_URL.
- Use an alphanumeric database password to avoid URL-encoding problems.
- Generate and store secrets in a password manager.
- Remove TEST_DATABASE_URL from the production .env.
- Do not email .env, upload it to OneDrive or commit it to GitHub.
- Keep AI disabled until the intended provider and production key are configured.

The current branch does not use ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD to create the first user. Installation must stop here unless the approved release fixes this.

## **7\. Validate and start Docker**

From C:\\OmegaApps\\OmegaDocumentCreator:

docker compose -f infra/docker/compose.yaml config

Read the output and confirm:

- The client-folder path is correct.
- No example passwords remain.
- PostgreSQL binds only to 127.0.0.1.
- The API binds only to 127.0.0.1.
- The frontend binds only to 127.0.0.1.

Start the application:

docker compose -f infra/docker/compose.yaml up -d --build

docker compose -f infra/docker/compose.yaml ps

All services should eventually show running or healthy.

Check the backend:

Invoke-WebRequest <http://127.0.0.1:8000/ready>

Inspect errors:

docker compose -f infra/docker/compose.yaml logs --tail 100 api

docker compose -f infra/docker/compose.yaml logs --tail 100 frontend

docker compose -f infra/docker/compose.yaml logs --tail 100 postgres

Do not continue if the API reports unsafe configuration, migration failures or no administrator account.

## **8\. Prepare the domain carefully**

Cloudflare must control the DNS zone used for the application.

Before changing the domain's nameservers, have the current website/DNS administrator verify that Cloudflare contains all existing:

- Website records.
- MX email records.
- SPF records.
- DKIM records.
- DMARC records.
- Any third-party verification records.

Changing nameservers without copying these records could interrupt the website or email.

## **9\. Create Cloudflare Access protection**

Create the protection before allowing staff to use the application.

In Cloudflare:

1. Open **Zero Trust**.
2. Create a Free organisation.
3. Go to **Access controls → Applications**.
4. Select **Create application**.
5. Select **Self-hosted and private**.
6. Add:

omega-app.omegafinancial.ie

1. Create an **Allow** policy.
2. Add the eight exact individual email addresses.
3. Select email one-time PIN as the permitted login method.
4. Set the Access session duration to seven days.
5. Ensure everyone not matching the policy is denied.

Cloudflare's 2026 interface may describe the email-code provider as Cloudflare's default identity provider rather than "One-time PIN". Use the option that sends a temporary authentication code to the approved email address.

Do not allow:

- Everyone.
- Any @omegafinancial.ie address.
- Shared addresses such as info@.
- An unrestricted email PIN rule.

Cloudflare's Free plan currently has a 50-user limit. [Cloudflare Zero Trust pricing](https://www.cloudflare.com/plans/zero-trust-services/) · [Self-hosted application setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/applications/http-apps/self-hosted-public-app/)

## **10\. Install Cloudflare Tunnel**

In the Cloudflare dashboard:

1. Go to **Networking → Tunnels**.
2. Select **Create tunnel**.
3. Name it:

omega-production

1. Select Windows as the connector environment.
2. Cloudflare will display a command containing a private tunnel token.
3. Copy that command.
4. Run it in PowerShell as Administrator on the office server.

It will resemble:

cloudflared.exe service install YOUR_PRIVATE_TUNNEL_TOKEN

Never put that token in GitHub, OneDrive, email or documentation.

Configure one public hostname:

| **Setting**      | **Value**                   |
| ---------------- | --------------------------- |
| Hostname         | omega-app.omegafinancial.ie |
| ---              | ---                         |
| Service type     | HTTP                        |
| ---              | ---                         |
| Internal address | <http://localhost:3000>     |
| ---              | ---                         |

Do not create a public API hostname. Do not publish ports 8000 or 5432.

Cloudflare recommends running cloudflared as a service so it starts automatically with Windows. [Create a Cloudflare Tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/create-remote-tunnel/) · [Run cloudflared as a service](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/as-a-service/)

## **11\. First sign-in and staff accounts**

Open:

<https://omega-app.omegafinancial.ie>

The correct sequence is:

1. Enter an authorised staff email.
2. Retrieve the Cloudflare email code.
3. Enter the code.
4. Reach the Omega login page.
5. Sign in using the first administrator account.
6. Change the initial administrator password immediately.
7. Create seven additional individual Omega accounts.
8. Assign the correct roles and client-access permissions.
9. Remove any test or default accounts.

If the first administrator does not exist, stop. Do not create a production administrator by manually editing PostgreSQL.

## **12\. Complete the go-live test**

Before using real client data, verify:

- An unapproved email cannot reach the Omega login screen.
- All eight approved emails can receive codes.
- Each employee has an individual Omega account.
- Login and logout work.
- Secure session cookies are used.
- A client can be created, saved, reopened and edited.
- Dependants remain saved after refreshing.
- Quotations remain saved after refreshing.
- Autosave does not duplicate clients.
- File upload and download work.
- Document generation and export work.
- Role restrictions work for each employee.
- A test file appears in the OneDrive web interface.
- The client folder remains locally available without internet.
- PostgreSQL and the API are unreachable from another computer.
- No router port forwarding exists.
- A complete backup can be restored on another computer.

Do not go live if any test fails.

## **13\. Restart test**

Restart the office PC.

After restarting:

1. Sign in to OmegaServer.
2. Confirm OneDrive is synchronising.
3. Confirm Docker Desktop has started.
4. Run:

Set-Location C:\\OmegaApps\\OmegaDocumentCreator

docker compose -f infra/docker/compose.yaml ps

Get-Service cloudflared

1. Confirm the Cloudflare tunnel is healthy.
2. Open the public application address from another computer.
3. Lock the server PC; do not sign out.

## **14\. Backups**

The backup must contain a matching set of:

- PostgreSQL database dump.
- Uploaded client files.
- Generated documents.
- Production .env.
- Restoration instructions.

Use:

- Daily encrypted backup.
- Separate encrypted offsite copy.
- Periodic disconnected copy.
- Quarterly restoration test.

OneDrive only synchronises the client folder. It does not back up PostgreSQL.

Because the current application's restoration process is unsafe, require the developer to provide and test an offline restore procedure before go-live.

## **15\. Updating the live installation**

Only deploy tagged GitHub releases.

Before every update:

1. Stop normal staff use.
2. Create and verify a complete backup.
3. Record the current tag and commit.
4. Fetch the new tag.
5. Switch to it.
6. Rebuild the containers.
7. Test the complete workflow.

Example:

Set-Location C:\\OmegaApps\\OmegaDocumentCreator

git status

git fetch --tags

git switch --detach v1.1.0

docker compose -f infra/docker/compose.yaml up -d --build

docker compose -f infra/docker/compose.yaml ps

Never configure the office PC to deploy automatically from main.

Development continues separately on another computer using feature branches and dummy data. GitHub must never contain client records, documents, databases, .env, backup archives or Cloudflare credentials.
